mods.name: Debug Menu
mods.author: Moon Sweepers Mods
mods.description:
Testing tools. In-game, open the pause menu (Esc) and a DEBUG panel appears on the right (F7 hides or shows it).

Unlimited money, +$10,000, unlimited suit energy, fly mode, empty or fill your vehicle's hopper, and spawn any vehicle in front of you, including vehicles added by other mods.

Meant for testing: it changes your save (money, vehicles). Host only: in someone else's crew it turns itself off, since the host controls money, time and vehicles.

mods.name: Hello World
mods.author: Moon Sweepers Mods
mods.description:
A tiny example mod. It shows a "Hello World mod loaded" label in the top-left corner for 30 seconds after the game starts, and logs a message whenever the main menu opens.

Use it as a starting point for your own mods: copy examples/HelloWorld in the repo and rename it.

mods.name: Better Belts
mods.author: MSML
mods.description:
Pneumatic tubes: glass tubes sunk into the ground that shoot capsules along up to 5x as fast as conveyor belts (10x in SETTINGS).

Build them with the Pneumatic tube card (Logistics) like belts, up to 90 m in one piece. They follow the ground over bumps and down hills, connect to belts, splitters, mergers and machines (rising out of the ground to meet them), and you can walk and drive over them. The Tube splitter and Tube merger cards build splitters and mergers sunk into the ground, so tube lines join them flush (and they rise to meet plain belts); aim at a tube to build one into it. A tube on its own runs at belt speed; put a Tube booster in the line (aim at a tube to build one into it) and the capsules after it are shot along at full speed. Boosters run on solar power like any machine (you'll see the blue power beam and hear them hiss). The pressure carries through tubes, splitters and mergers (not belts or machines) and fades after about 80 m, so put the next booster where the tube turns yellow.

The rings on the tubes show the pressure: green is full speed, yellow is fading, red is belt speed. They glow brighter while you're building. A colour-blind palette is in SETTINGS, along with the speed, range, prices and power.

Tubes never stop: losing a booster or power only slows them to belt speed. Removing a tube deletes the capsules in it. Remove the mod and tubes become plain belts again. Everyone in a crew needs the mod.

mods.name: Hex Harvester
mods.author: MSML
mods.description:
A new vehicle, sold in the garage for $100,000: the Hex Harvester. A six-wheeled harvester with a hex-glass cab, a glass hex silo that visibly fills with dust as you clean, and a 25 m truss-mounted sweeper head with five brush pods. It clears a whole hex in one pass.

It runs on the game's own vehicle code, so driving, cleaning, the hopper, unloading, upgrades, lights and sounds all work like the other vehicles. Its price and upgrade prices can be changed in SETTINGS. It's too big for the garage hall, so it's delivered in front of the garage.

Saves stay safe: if you remove the mod, a bought Hex Harvester just disappears from the garage until the mod is back. Everyone in a crew needs the mod.

mods.name: MoonFixerUpper
mods.author: MSML
mods.description:
Fixes for problems in the game itself. Each fix can be turned off in SETTINGS (here, or MOD SETTINGS in the pause menu).

Crew dust keeps up (crewmates): when several players are cleaning, the dust behind your own vehicle no longer lags seconds behind. Your game cleans everyone's strokes in one queue, and with wide heads it overflows, so your strokes waited behind everyone else's or were dropped. While it's backed up, other players' strokes far from you (60 m, adjustable) are left to the host's dust sync, and yours are cleaned straight away. The host is never affected.

Moon Sweepers 1.0.5 fixed "Could not pack a capsule" itself, so the earlier fix for it was removed.

mods.name: MoonSweeper+
mods.author: MSML
mods.description:
The official MSML quality-of-life mod: small fixes for everyday annoyances. Every fix can be turned on or off with SETTINGS (here, or MOD SETTINGS in the pause menu).

Vehicle camera: the camera stays where you point it while driving instead of snapping back behind the vehicle. Turn on auto recenter to bring the snap-back back, with your own delay.
